correctness.rationale: All 65,536 subsets of sixteen Boolean vertices are exhaustively checked by an exact maximal-index recurrence and, independently, by direct inclusion among all 256 scalene triples. The recurrence adds exactly the triples with the new largest-index vertex. A separate parity-Hamming count gives the candidate formula and interpretable equality cases. Every mask is checked against its cardinality minimum and the asserted equality predicate; integer arithmetic and full source are included. The code was executed successfully from the actual standalone file. No infinite or untested extension is claimed.

originality.rationale: The proposed quantity is the cardinality-by-cardinality minimum of all-scalene triple defects among sixteen fixed Hamming vertices, including sharp antipodal equality classes. Ionin proves Hamming-space cardinality and two-distance structural bounds, and Yi proves unrestricted Euclidean isosceles-set bounds, neither of which supplies the defect-minimum profile. The closest available published four-cube entries concern different mathematical invariants. Actual subject-specific query results and primary material were compared by implication. Worldwide historical priority remains provisional because unindexed finite tables may exist.
residual_risks: A niche unindexed tabulation of 4-cube scalene-triplet counts could predate this calculation; broad search and full-text comparisons do not certify world-first priority.
The full text of all geometrically adjacent published four-cube studies was not exhaustively inspected; their advertised invariants differ and provide no known domination.
The result is finite-dimensional and only the sixteen-vertex cube; this is an intentional, explicitly stated scientific limit.

value.rationale: Exact sharp supersaturation for an inherently natural geometric property: every cardinality in the first nontrivial parity half-cube (the four-cube), a closed formula, precise antipodal-collision threshold, and complete equality classification for all cardinalities six and above. These quantify forced violations beyond maximum isosceles subsets, rather than merely recomputing a known maximum or arbitrary slice. The finite benchmark is directly relevant to the Hamming-space isosceles problem and can serve as a check for future dimensional stability results.
